hints.junior: Short cache lifetimes feel safe, but they mean everyone re-downloads the same unchanged file over and over. That's the opposite of what caching is for.
hints.mid: Same-named asset + short Cache-Control is a tradeoff you don't have to make once hashing enters the picture.
hints.staff: The real bug here is that HTML and its hashed assets need opposite caching policies, one mutable pointer, one immutable payload.

hints.junior: Toggle between the two modes and watch which requests actually hit the network on the second and third simulated visit.
hints.mid: The fixed mode's request log should go quiet after the first load until the hash itself changes.
hints.staff: The broken mode's 'stale after deploy' state is a 200 from cache, not an error, that's exactly why it's hard to catch in monitoring.

hints.junior: The filename itself becomes the cache key. Change the file, change the name, and the old cached copy just stops being requested.
hints.mid: max-age=31536000 plus immutable only makes sense once the URL is a pure function of the content.
hints.staff: This turns cache invalidation, notoriously hard, into a non-problem: there's nothing to invalidate, only a new URL to start requesting.

hints.junior: The HTML file is the one exception, it always needs a short cache lifetime so the browser can learn the new hashed filenames.
hints.mid: no-cache on the HTML entry point forces a cheap revalidation (a 304) on every load instead of skipping the request entirely.
hints.staff: A service worker's cache lifecycle doesn't inherit HTTP Cache-Control for free, if one exists, it needs this same discipline applied on purpose.

sections.junior: Hey! Today's case is about a static file that never changes name between deploys, so browsers end up re-downloading it constantly, or worse, serving a stale copy after you ship a fix.
The fix is to bake a content hash into the filename, so the URL itself changes the moment the file does, and cache that URL forever with no risk.
Try the short-lived cache mode first, then switch to hashed and immutable, and watch how many requests actually go out on the repeat visits.
Hash your asset filenames, cache them forever, and keep the HTML that points to them on a short lifetime so it always finds the latest hash.
